messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Using rqtl with GWAS data
parts:
R/qtl isn't appropriate for GWAS data; it is for the analysis of crosses.

karl

On Apr 24, 2013, at 8:46 AM, Luisa Pallares <lfpal...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Karl,
> I work with GWAS data in mouse and I've found some very interesting options in rqtl that I would like to explore with my data.
>
> I have a very dense marker coverage of my genome (~200.000 snps, ~1snp every 4Kb), and therefore I dont need to perform the snp imputation step. I took a look into the manual and it specifies that all analysis require the output of calc.genoprob function.
> The first thing I thought was tricking rqtl formatting my data with the format of the output of calc.genoprob, but it says the object is to complex to print... so I couldnt see the format that I need.
>
> Is there a way in which I can import my genotype data and then rqtl can read it as its own?
>
> And the other critical question... can rqtl deal with population relatedness in the sample? is it able to correct for that?
>
> Thanks!
> Luisa.
